title: stripe prefetch + planar kernel router: MQA/Llama throughput optimizations
author: Samantha Ortiz
release_notes:
- Add stripe-prefetch scheduler to reduce KV cache thrash for MQA workloads.
- Introduce planar-kernel router heuristics for memory-layout-aware kernel selection.
- Improved continuous batching behavior when token-length variance is high for Llama family models.
description:
Motivation: We observe recurring throughput regressions on MQA workloads for Llama-family models when sequence-length variance and multi-query attention interact with our default kernel selection. Two measurable pain points: (1) frequent small KV cache misses when token generations cross stripe boundaries, and (2) suboptimal kernel tiling choices for planar weight layouts that some Qwen/Mistral/Llama variants expose. This PR adds a lightweight stripe-prefetch scheduler and a planar-kernel routing heuristic that picks kernels based on observed layout and upcoming stripe patterns.

Summary of changes (single-line list): stripe-prefetch scheduler, planar kernel router, small scheduler API additions, new microbench harness for stripe workloads, unit+integration tests, documentation for tuning knobs.

What the patch does (detailed): The stripe-prefetch scheduler tracks the active KV stripe window for each session and enqueues prefetches for the next N stripes when continuous-batching is used and the workload matches MQA characteristics (multi-head quantized attention with per-head stride > 1). Prefetching is conservative: it is only issued when the current latency SLO isn't filling and when memory pressure estimator indicates a <15% overhead risk. The planar-kernel router adds a lightweight feature extractor that scores candidate kernels using (1) the weight memory layout (planar vs packed), (2) sequence length percentile, and (3) runtime tile fit (L2/L3 footprints). The router falls back to existing kernel routing for unknown/rare layouts.

APIs and config: two new config flags under runtime.tuning: runtime.tuning.stripe_prefetch.enabled (default true), runtime.tuning.stripe_prefetch.max_prefetch_stripes (default 2), runtime.tuning.planar_router.enabled (default true), and runtime.tuning.planar_router.score_threshold (default 0.12). These defaults were chosen after microbench tuning across common GPU families.

Benchmarks: Microbench harness (bench/stripe_mqa_harness) runs a 4k-16k token mix with 8-shot prompt patterns. On A100-40GB we measured: throughput +19% (p50 for batching throughput) for MQA-Llama-70B-quant profile, +12% for MQA-Mistral-7B in mixed-length traces. Median latency change at p50 was +1.8ms (within SLO) and p99 shifted by +6ms in worst cases when prefetching hit memory pressure; the policy prevented >10% p99 regressions in tuned settings. More details in commits.

Compatibility: Non-breaking by default. Flags can be switched off. Prefetch is session-scoped so cold-start behavior unchanged. We added a fallback to current kernel chooser if the new heuristics produce a score below threshold.

Testing: Unit tests for scheduler logic and router scoring (tests/runtime/test_stripe_prefetch.py, tests/runtime/test_planar_router.py), integration tests that run end-to-end generated traffic in the bench container (CI job bench/stripe-mqa), and a stress run that validated memory pressure gating.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc & perf plan discussed in ENG-4321
- [x] Microbench results checked in bench/outputs
- [x] Unit & integration tests added
- [x] Runtime flags exposed and documented
- [x] Backwards-compatible defaults

Related: PRs that touched kernel routing previously (see refs in commits). Linked support ticket SUP-1182 where a customer reported repeated stalls on Llama-MQA workloads.

Notes for reviewers: focus on (a) correctness of memory-pressure gating, (b) potential contention with existing batching path, (c) kernel routing thresholds. Perf graphs and raw numbers are in bench/outputs/38421/*.

review_comments:
Ravi Kumar: can you justify the default max_prefetch_stripes=2? We saw marginal gains beyond 2 but risk higher memory use.
S. Ortiz: We ran grid search across 0-4 stripes; 2 gives best median throughput with acceptable memory on A100/RTX6000. I added bench/outputs/38421/prefetch_grid.csv to show this.

Elena Park: The router scoring is neat but I'm worried about cost of scoring per-request. Can we cache scores per model-version?
S. Ortiz: yes — we add a per-model-version score cache with LRU expiry (30 minutes) in commit 5 which addresses this.

Jonas Meyer: I hit a race on high concurrency where prefetch queue could be double-enqueued; fixed in last commit.

R. Kumar: Approved after the race fix and addition of the LRU score cache.
Elena Park: Approved.
ci: Initial CI: lint failed (flake8 formatting) -> fixed in commit 4; unit tests passed; bench job required a rerun (resource quota) and passed on second run. Full CI status: pass (all checks green).

post_merge_notes:
Monitoring: Added perf alert rule 'mqa.stripe_prefetch_mem_pressure' (alerts when prefetch gated >30% of sessions and p99 latency increased >10%). We'll monitor for 2 weeks.
Rollback: flip runtime.tuning.stripe_prefetch.enabled=false if any widespread issues.
